title: Sharded cost attribution and quota enforcement for embeddings + structured tool outputs
creator: Asha Gupta
description:
Problem: Non-chat endpoints that perform embeddings, rerank, and structured tool invocations produce composite billable events that are currently mis-attributed across customer quotas and rate windows when calls are sharded, retried, or partially succeed. Symptoms we've observed: duplicate charges for speculative prefetch, undercounting for batched rerank fan-outs, and quota exhaustion due to incorrect per-call rounding. Impact: unexpected billing spikes and hard quota blocks for high-throughput vector workloads and structured output pipelines.

Goals: 1) Produce deterministic, idempotent cost entries for embedding and structured-tool call flows even when requests are retried or split. 2) Enforce customer quotas and rate windows in a sharded serving environment without over-blocking or under-counting. 3) Provide a clear migration path and visibility for customers so we can surface reconciled deltas in billing dashboards.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change tokenization or per-model pricing tiers; it is focused on correct accounting and quota semantics for non-chat endpoints and tool calls (embeddings, rerank, toolcall wrappers, structured output endpoints).

High-level approach: - Introduce a lightweight request fingerprint (fingerprint format: hex of trace_id + stable-call-seq) attached to every downstream shard and cached result. - Move cost emission to a single coordinator responsible for deduplicating fingerprinted events and emitting a single billable record per logical request. - Implement "shard-window" quota enforcement: the coordinator reserves planned token units for the logical request at acceptance time, then releases or finalizes them on completion/partial-failure. - Add a fallback charge reconciliation path that can take speculative prefetch/partial-success records and fold them into a single reconciled charge within a bounded reconciliation window (currently 10 minutes).

Telemetry and observability: new metrics at the coordinator level: fingerprint_dedupe_rate, coordinator_reserve_success, coordinator_release_count, reconciliation_adjustments_total. Add a dashboard tile in Console showing reconciled vs emitted charges by endpoint and customer.

Backward compatibility and migration: the coordinator will run in front of existing shard pools behind a feature flag per region. For 2 weeks of canary we will run in double-write mode: emit both the legacy per-shard records and the deduplicated coordinator record (tagging legacy records with legacy_emitted=true). Post verification, legacy path will be turned off and we will surface the net delta in billing UI for affected customers (reason codes and per-customer delta).

Testing: unit tests for fingerprint collision bounds, load-test harness with synthetic fanout patterns, staged e2e with internal billing sandbox, and smoke-run for quota enforcement on high-throughput embedding jobs.

Rollout plan: 1) Implement coordinator and gate behind feature-flag (week 1). 2) Canary in us-west with double-write and dashboard monitoring (week 2). 3) Gradual ramp to 20% of traffic in region and verify adjustments <0.5% (week 3). 4) Global rollout and legacy off (week 4).

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator emits exactly one billable record (tagged) for 99.999% of synthetic non-chat requests in the load harness for 1h at peak QPS.
Quota enforcement uses reserved units so no customer sees a spuriously decreased available quota during sharded execution; observed reservation success rate >= 99.9% under test traffic.
Reconciliation window collapses speculative prefetch partial charges into a net single adjustment; reconciliation_adjustments_total should be <0.5% of emitted charges in canary.
Console shows reconciled delta per-customer and a PRD linking to the billing adjustments report for support teams.
No increase in 5xx errors attributable to coordinator path during canary; latency p95 increase <= 5ms at coordinator insertion point.
